title: Wear-IT Study Specification
description: This specification contains all the needed information to both run a study using the Wear-IT framework. This includes all the needed information to make reproducible and replicable codebooks for complex designs.

examples.Study.Name: Recovery Community Center Project
examples.authors: Jane Smith, John Doe, Emily R. Johnson
examples.abstract: This study examined daily stress and recovery patterns among adults attending a recovery community center. Participants completed ecological momentary assessments four times daily over 14 days across two bursts.

AI.Disclosure.description: List of AI-generated characteristics and the model used to generate each one. Supports multi-agent/multi-model provenance, or a single entry with Characteristic='All' if one model generated everything.

Characteristic.description: The specific data element, section, or design aspect that was AI generated (e.g. 'study design', 'survey text', 'data analysis code', 'summary narrative', 'figure captions'). Use 'All' if a single model was responsible for the entire output.

Model.description: String indicating what generative AI model was used to produce this characteristic

Study.Name.description: Human readable long name for a study

authors.description: String of all people to be credited for this study. This will appear in the authors section of a generated codebook.

funding.description: String containing relevant funding info for the study

abstract.description: String containing qualitative description of the study. This could include main study objectives, relevant findings, study population etc.

schedules.description: Array containing schedules for a study

children.description: Nested child schedules (e.g. bursts) that belong to this schedule as a whole, as opposed to a single event within it — see the 'children' property under an individual event's extensions for that case.

alarm.description: ISO-8601 timestamp at which the alarm should fire.

until.description: End of the recurrence. ISO-8601 date-time or date string (see dateTime/date definitions).

start.description: ISO-8601 date-time or date (see dateTime/date definitions).

end.description: ISO-8601 date-time or date (see dateTime/date definitions).

start.description: Start date/time of the event. ISO-8601 date-time or date (see dateTime/date definitions).

end.description: End date/time of the event (exclusive). ISO-8601 date-time or date (see dateTime/date definitions).

private.description: Whether the event details should be hidden from public feeds.

overrides.description: Per-instance modifications or cancellations (keyed by ISO date / date-time string).

extensions.description: Vendor-specific extensions applicable to this event.

User.Specified.description: Boolean indicating whether the timing window is user specified

Timing.Type.description: Type of timing. Fixed means, no variation in timing window. Random is drawing a random sample from a time period, triggered is based on set rules more in depth than just random in a time period.

Trigger.Info.description: Contains the trigger logic if it exists for a given window.

Conditional.Source.description: Source of measurement to trigger conditional

Conditional.Threshold.description: Threshold is the preset value being compared to the user response.

Conditional.Type.description: Conditional type is the comparator (in order: =, <=, >=, <, >, !=)

children.description: Nested child schedules (e.g. bursts) that belong to this specific event, as opposed to the schedule as a whole — see the schedule-level 'children' property for that case.

Survey.Name.description: Name of the survey delivered by this schedule, referencing a Survey.Name value elsewhere in this document. Optional — some schedules (e.g. passive/sensor sync, administrative reminders) deliver no survey. JSON Schema cannot verify the referenced survey actually exists; any agent or tool generating or consuming this data must independently confirm it resolves to a real Survey.Name in the same study spec.

surveys.title: Survey Specifications
surveys.description: Array of survey specifications within this burst. Each survey represents a distinct instrument delivered to participants. May be empty if no surveys have been defined yet.

questions.title: Question Specification
questions.description: Contains all the information needed to specify a question or variable in a survey, observation, or passive data collection context.

items.$comment: Parent, Conditional.Master.Item.ID, Conditional.Child.Item.ID, Conditional.Fail.Item.ID, and Trigger.Info.Conditional.Source are string references to other items' Item.ID values elsewhere in this document. JSON Schema cannot verify that a referenced ID actually exists — passing validation does NOT guarantee these references are valid. Any agent or tool generating or consuming this data must independently confirm that every referenced Item.ID resolves to a real item in the same study spec.

examples.Question.Long.Name: Perceived Stress Item 1
examples.Question.Text: How stressed have you felt in the past hour?
examples.Question.Description: A self-report measure of perceived stress on a scale from 0 (not at all) to 100 (extremely).
examples.Question.Type.Display.Name: Slider

Question.ID.description: Name of the variable as it appears in the dataset. Identifies a question within a single survey — unique per survey (e.g. a morning survey and an evening survey use different Question.IDs even for the 'same' item), but shared across repeated deliveries of that same survey (e.g. the same morning survey repeated over 10 days keeps the same Question.ID each day).

Question.Long.Name.description: Human readable name for the variable

Question.Text.description: Exact text of the question as presented to the participant. Only applicable for survey questions.

Question.Description.description: Description of the variable in layman's terms. If layman's terms are not possible, provide a citation to a longer explanation.

Question.Type.Display.Name.description: How the data was obtained. Must match one of the supported Wear-IT display types.

oneOf.description: User can write in any text they want.
Displays information to the user only. Does not collect a response.
User selects exactly one option from a list.
User selects any number of options from a list.
Displays multiple VAS sliders simultaneously, one response per slider.
Displays a single VAS slider for one response.
User selects a time scale value using a VAS slider.
Marks the start of a block grouping questions together.
Marks the end of a block.

examples.definition: Less than five minutes (just stopped in)

definition.description: Human-readable label for the response value.

Parent.description: Item ID of the parent item. NOTE: This is different than the conditional master which points to the item which if successful, delivers the current. Parent may point to a block many questions up.

Conditional.Info.description: Contains all the conditional info for a question

Conditional.Child.Item.ID.description: Item ID for the successful child of the current question.

Conditional.Fail.Item.ID.description: Item ID for the fail child of the current question.

Conditional.Master.Item.ID.description: Item ID for the parent of the current question.

Conditional.Threshold.description: Threshold is the preset value being compared to the user response.

Conditional.Type.description: Conditional type is the comparator (in order: =, <=, >=, <, >, !=)

Data.Type.description: The type of data captured by this variable. Oldname: Result.Type

Item.ID.description: Item ID for this question. Identifies a single question definition, reused across repeated deliveries of the same survey (e.g. the same Item.ID appears across all 10 days a morning survey is repeated).

data.title: Data Specification (Column Vector Format)
data.description: All fields are stored as column vectors (arrays), where each position corresponds to a participant/record in the dataset.

Alert.Times.description: Each entry is a participant-level array of alert times, as ISO-8601 date-time strings.

Survey.Start.description: Timestamp the survey was started, as an ISO-8601 date-time string.

Survey.Date.Completed.description: Timestamp the survey was completed, as an ISO-8601 date-time string.

Survey.Date.Submitted.description: Timestamp the survey was submitted, as an ISO-8601 date-time string.

itemMap.title: Item Map Repo
itemMap.description: This specification contains all the needed information to describe a single item or scale used within the Wear-IT framework, including its conceptual, psychometric, and delivery properties.

examples.Item.Text: How stressed did you feel today?
examples.Modeling.Characteristics: Typically used as an outcome variable; no transformation required
examples.Scale.Name: Perceived Stress Scale
examples.Top.Level.Question: Indicate to what extent you...
examples.Definition: Never, Almost Never, Sometimes, Fairly Often, Very Often
examples.Article.Title: A global measure of perceived stress
examples.Citation: Cohen, S., Kamarck, T., & Mermelstein, R. (1983). https://doi.org/10.2307/2136404
examples.notes: Standard PSS-10 item; time stem adapted from original

Item.Text.description: Exact text of the item as presented.

Conceptualization.description: What construct or concept does this item measure or represent?

Modeling.Characteristics.description: Usual modeling characteristics or how this item is typically used in analysis (e.g. predictor, outcome, mediator, covariate). For example, reaction time is often log transformed.

Validated.description: Whether this item is part of a statistically validated measure.

Scale.Name.description: Name of the scale this item belongs to.

Parent.Scale.description: Name of the parent scale if this item belongs to a subscale.

Sub.Scale.description: Name of the subscale this item belongs to, if applicable.

scaleOrItem.description: Whether this entry represents a full scale or a single item.

Scale.Type.description: The type of scale this item uses (e.g. Likert, VAS, semantic differential, binary, forced choice).

Scoring.description: How this item or scale is scored, including any summing, averaging, or weighting rules (e.g. sum score, factor scores, weighted sum scores).

Reverse.Coded.description: Whether this item is reverse coded or otherwise transformed before use.

Transformation.description: Description of any transformation applied to this item beyond simple reverse coding.

Identifying.Info.description: Whether this item potentially contains personally identifying information.

Data.Type.description: Type of data this item produces.

Time.Stem.description: The time reference embedded in the item (e.g. 'in the past week', 'right now', 'today').

Top.Level.Question.description: The top-level or parent question this item falls under, if it is a sub-item.

Definition.description: Nominal or text-based response options or categories.

Delivery.Mechanism.description: How the item is delivered to the participant (e.g. mobile app, paper, wearable, passive sensor, interviewer).

Delivery.Frequency.description: How frequently this item is delivered (e.g. once daily, every 4 hours, event-contingent).

Citation.description: DOI citation for the item or scale source, or APA formatted citation.

notes.description: Any additional notes about this item.

screenshotsURL.description: URL of the study's bulk screenshot retrieval endpoint.

blockMap.description: Flattened delivery order of all items across surveys. Used to reconstruct intended question flow independent of data arrival order.
